methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $14M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
The ePlane Company is a Series B transportation venture that has raised $14M+ and is currently seeking $40–50M in new capital. The broader transportation sector comprises eight private peers of varying scale and stage, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, and Parallel Systems; no directly comparable public companies exist in this frontier-tech subset.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised ($14M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Series B step-up multiplier of 1.9x yields an implied valuation of $27M. Peer-median analysis was not feasible due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the Transportation sector; the existing peer set spans divergent scales and development phases, making narrow cross-sectional analysis unreliable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $23M (low) to $31M (median–high), centered at $27M. This range reflects the limitations of a single-method triangulation. Key uncertainties include the stage-progression multiplier's applicability to a company in early revenue/prototype phases, the absence of direct peer benchmarks at equivalent scale and development milestones, and the broader risk profile of frontier transportation ventures. Investors should treat this as a directional anchor rather than a tight band; updated analysis incorporating revenue traction, technology validation milestones, or narrower peer sets would strengthen conviction.
